messages:
maria: FYI - ACME reported large embedding latency spikes this morning. They say requests from eu-west keep hitting our us-east embedding pool and causing cold starts.
aj: do we have a correlation id or example request?
maria: correlation=cor_9f3a; snippet from customer: `POST /v1/embeddings model=text-embedding-3 size=1536 region=eu-west-1` headers: `x-rw-region: eu-west-1`, but our access logs show routed to `embed-us-east-1a`.
ingrid: that's odd. Routing should honor region preference unless capacity constraints triggered spillover. any error codes in responses?
maria: responses were 200 but with large tail latency (p95 ~1.2s -> usual ~140ms). customer also saw a burst of 429s earlier.
support-bot: incident created: INC-210555 - Embeddings egress mismatch (auto-detected routing anomalies). Assigned to #eng-infra.
aj: looking at router logs now. I see a sudden capacity signal from eu-west pool at 2105551200 -> we forwarded 37% to fallback. But I also see routing table entries with stale weight for us-east due to deployment during autoscale.
bob_oncall: can we reproduce locally? steps we used last time: send 1k concurrent small embeds with `region=eu-west-1` and watch routing decisions.
ingrid: quick check: model vector dim is 1536 in customer's request. Any chance they switched model and we returned different dims causing retries? that would be another path.
maria: customer confirmed they were on expected model. They did see duplicated requests from their side when timeouts hit.
elaine: I pulled the queue metrics: eu-west embed queue length spiked at 2105551185, throughput dipped, then routing policy started egressing to us-east at 2105551198 with a high weight. But there were also cold-starts in us-east because we hadn't prewarmed enough for that burst.
aj: root cause likely a combination: autoscaler in eu-west under-provisioned for the sudden burst + routing policy aggressively spilled over to us-east, which had cold-start churn -> increased latency and a few 429s. Also observed an incorrect health reaction from one instance bumping weight erroneously.
maria: customer asks for mitigation and billing concerns (they got charged additional inter-region egress).
aj: mitigation: 1) immediate: add temporary sticky routing to prefer eu-west for this customer and disable spillover for 10m. 2) mid: adjust autoscaler thresholds and prewarm policy for eu-west embed pool. 3) post: audit routing weight decay bug.
bob_oncall: applied temporary sticky rule for customer ACME (CID: acct-acme-73) at 2105551255 -> requests should be pinned to eu-west for next 15m.
ingrid: can someone capture the exact header that caused the mis-eval? I want the raw request sample for replay.
maria: pasted raw (redacted keys): `POST /v1/embeddings \nAuthorization: Bearer ****\nX-RW-REGION: eu-west-1\nX-RW-CUSTOMER: acct-acme-73\nContent-Type: application/json\n{ "model": "text-embedding-3", "input": ["foo"] }`
aj: thanks. I'll replay at lower QPS to validate routing after sticky rule.
support-bot: update INC-210555 -> sticky rule applied, monitoring enabled.
elaine: action items recorded: (a) infra to backport autoscaler tune -> owner @aj, ETA 48h; (b) fix routing weight decay bug -> owner @ingrid, ETA 72h; (c) billing review for inter-region egress for ACME -> owner @maria, ETA 24h.
maria: ACME emailed saying latency improved after 2105551260. They still want a short postmortem and confirmation about billing credits.
aj: replay results: with sticky rule, routing stays in eu-west and p95 drops back to ~160ms. No 429s. Will start autoscaler tune PR.
ingrid: I'll start a small test harness to reproduce scenario with synthetic burst and confirm weight-decay fix addresses misrouting.
bob_oncall: leaving a note on the customer ticket: link to INC-210555, include correlation cor_9f3a and sticky-rule id SR-210555-A.
maria: thanks team. I'll coordinate billing and customer comms. :thumbsup:
aj: filing followup ticket on infra board: RW-OPS-emb-route-210555.
support-bot: incident INC-210555 status -> monitoring: steady, assigned: aj, ingrid, maria, elaine.
